To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
the human liver cell line Hep-G-2 is capable of supporting production of infectious DHBV.
we have produced infectious duck hepatitis B (DHBV), the avian homologue of the mammalian hepatitis B virus (HBV), in a human liver cell line, Hep-G2.

we have established a transfection system in which human hepatoma cells can be infected with DHBV and that we have used this system to study the role of the DHBV precore protein in viral replication and pathogenicity in ducks.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the molecular genetics and molecular biology of the duck hepatitis B virus, which is a member of the family Hepadnaviridae.
the development of new strategies in the fight against hepatitis viruses.
the development of new methods for the study of hepatitis B virus and the development of new vaccines.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
DHBV is a good model to study HBV.
the DHBV transfectants are able to produce infectious virus, which can establish DHBV infection in ducks.
DHBV is a good candidate for a model to study the pathogenesis of HBV infection.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have successfully developed a new system to study the molecular biology of the DHBV genome and its gene expression.
the DHBV transfectant system can be used for studying the molecular biology of DHBV and its interactions with host cells and for the development of vaccines and antiviral agents.
we have developed a system to study DHBV in vitro, and we have shown that the DHBV DNA is able to infect ducks in vivo.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the DHBV transfectant cell lines provide a new system to study the molecular mechanisms of DHBV replication and the molecular pathogenesis of DHBV infection.
the DHBV transgenic duck model is a useful system for studying the biology of HBV infection and HBV-related diseases.
the HepG2-DHBV system is a useful model for studying DHBV infection and for the development of new anti-DHBV strategies.
